title: Sales Transcripts Into CRM, Two Passes Only
description: A two-pass workflow turning sales call transcripts into structured CRM payloads and grounded follow-up emails: forced tool use, Pydantic validation, MEDDIC fields with confidence levels, and why the email can only read the JSON.

sources.title: Sales Call Transcript to CRM Update

lines.text: Forty-minute discovery call. Rep hangs up, opens CRM, types: good call, they are interested, send deck.
Classic.
Three weeks later the deal dies. Nobody remembers the compliance objection or the economic buyer's name.
The information existed. It was in the transcript. Nobody extracted it in time.
Three weeks later nobody can reconstruct why the deal stalled.
The rep quit. Their notes say good call. That is all anyone has.
This project ensures the transcript itself becomes the CRM record, not the rep memory.

sections.title: Why two passes instead of one?

lines.text: This project turns transcripts into structured CRM updates and drafted emails.
CRM payload captures deal stage, MEDDIC fields, blockers, competitors, action items as typed JSON.
Email drafts from rep's voice but grounds strictly in the payload.
One call could do both. Save half the tokens.
Tried it. Version zero produced an email referencing a Workday comparison sheet the prospect explicitly declined.
Email pulled details directly from transcript, bypassing structure. Two passes enforce dependency: email sees only validated JSON.
Input is a raw transcript file. Output is validated JSON and a drafted email.
MEDDIC framework captures six dimensions: Metrics, Economic buyer, Decision criteria, Decision process, Identify pain, Champion.
Why MEDDIC specifically? Why not BANT or SPICED?
MEDDIC works well for complex B2B sales where multiple stakeholders matter. It maps naturally to structured fields.

sections.title: Forced tool use and confidence levels

lines.text: Pass one uses Claude with forced tool use. Model must invoke a defined signature producing JSON.
Pydantic validates. On failure, one retry, then refuse.
MEDDIC: Metrics, Economic buyer, Decision criteria, Decision process, Identify pain, Champion.
Each field carries confidence: high, medium, low, or null.
High means direct quote supports it. Low means inference. Null means insufficient information.
Why confidence levels, not just populated or empty?
Downstream users need to know what to trust. High-confidence champion drives action. Low-confidence guess triggers verification.
Forced tool use means the model must call a defined function signature rather than producing free-form text.
Function schema defines every MEDDIC field with types, descriptions, and allowed values.
Confidence levels add nuance: high means direct quote supports it verbatim, medium means clear paraphrase, low means inference.
Null means the transcript simply lacks information. Not unknown; absent from source data.
How do you distinguish low-confidence inference from hallucination?
Low-confidence fields must include a notes value explaining the reasoning. A bare low-confidence guess with no justification fails validation.
Pass two receives only the validated JSON object. It never sees the original transcript.
Email prompt says draft follow-up grounded exclusively in these facts. Any detail not present in JSON must not appear.
This architectural separation is the core insight. The email literally cannot hallucinate details the extraction rejected.
Clean discovery: well-run call. Most MEDDIC fields populate high-confidence with direct quotes.
Messy negotiation: late-stage check-in. Prospect hedges. Economic buyer null, decision criteria null, confidence drops to low.
Notes field surfaces soft signals: potential anti-champion, momentum risk.
Honest gaps are the feature.
Exactly. A CRM of confident guesses is worse than one with honest blanks.
Pass two drafts email from validated payload only. It writes naturally but cannot invent details.
Clean discovery call example.
Transcript shows prospect saying we process about forty thousand invoices monthly, manual AP takes twelve days.
Metrics field populates high confidence: forty thousand monthly volume, twelve-day cycle time.
Economic buyer identified: CFO signed off on evaluation budget. Direct quote supports it. High confidence.
Champion: VP of Operations championing internally. Named explicitly. High confidence.
Decision criteria mentions integration with existing ERP and security review. Medium confidence, paraphrased not quoted.
Now messy negotiation call.
Prospect says things are probably fine, we have other priorities right now, maybe revisit next quarter.
Economic buyer: null. Nobody named. Decision criteria: null. No specifics given.
Champion confidence drops to low. Notes field reads: soft signals suggest competing priorities, potential anti-champion in finance.
Deal stage downgrades from proposal to nurture. Email drafts accordingly: brief check-in, no aggressive ask.
Forty-minute transcript: eight thousand words, eleven thousand tokens.
Pass one input plus output: twenty thousand tokens with Claude Sonnet.
Pass two: validated JSON plus prompt, three thousand tokens.
Combined cost per call: pennies. Compare to fifteen minutes of manual CRM update.
Validation retry rate nears zero on clean transcripts. Messy inputs trigger more failures. Budget is one retry.
Token accounting per processing run.
Forty-minute transcript averages eight thousand spoken words, roughly eleven thousand tokens.
Pass one input: transcript plus function schema plus system instructions, approximately fourteen thousand tokens total input.
Pass one output: structured JSON with all MEDDIC fields, typically one thousand tokens.
Using Claude Sonnet pricing: input at three dollars per million tokens, output at fifteen dollars per million.
Pass one cost: approximately six cents. Pass two input is smaller, output shorter. Total under ten cents per call processed.
Compare to fifteen minutes of rep time manually updating CRM at a loaded hourly rate of sixty dollars: fifteen dollars.
Transcript enters. Forced tool call produces raw JSON. Validation with one retry.
Validated payload feeds pass two. Email generates grounded in payload facts only.
Output writes to simulated CRM keyed by call identifier. Every field traces to quote or marked inference.
Complete pipeline once more.
Transcript enters. Forced tool call produces JSON with all MEDDIC fields and confidence levels.
Pydantic validates types and constraints. One retry if validation fails. Refuse if still broken.
Validated payload feeds pass two exclusively. Email drafts from payload facts only, in rep voice.
Both outputs save to simulated CRM keyed by call identifier. Every field traces to quote or marked inference.
Speaker diarization errors merge two people into one label. Contradictory attributes attributed to same person. Fix proper diarization upstream.
Prospect sarcasm misreads as enthusiasm. High-confidence positive sentiment on stalled deal. Fix: hedging vocabulary lowers confidence.
CRM schema changes break existing payloads. Fix: schema versioning with migration path.
Pending: who reviews before commit? Can reps edit and does that feed back? What privacy consent covers recorded calls?
More subtle failure modes.
Multiple speakers use similar language. Diarization confuses who said what.
Signal: contradictory attributes attributed to same person. Champion and anti-champion merged. Fix upstream diarization quality.
Sarcasm or politeness masks disagreement. Prospect says interesting idea meaning no.
Signal: high positive sentiment followed by deal stalling. Fix hedging vocabulary detection lowers confidence.
CRM schema evolves. New required field added after deployment.
Signal: validation errors spike. Fix versioned schemas with migration path for existing records.
Pending: who reviews before CRM commit? Can reps edit extractions and does editing improve future prompts? Privacy consent for recorded calls?
Can you distinguish direct quote from inference in every field?
Does your second pass access anything the first did not validate?
When ambiguous, does confidence drop or does the system guess confidently anyway?
Fourth: if the prospect later disputes what was said, can you show the exact quote supporting each CRM field?
Fifth: does your system handle a transcript where the rep talks ninety percent of the time?
That usually means no discovery happened. Most fields should be null.
Self-test: prospect says budget is probably fine, subject to finance. What MEDDIC field, what confidence, why?
Next time: validating messy CSV data from enterprise clients and writing the email that builds trust while surfacing problems.
Could this integrate live during the call instead of after?
Real-time extraction changes latency requirements significantly. Worth prototyping but different problem.
